title: Grokipedia vs Wikipedia: An LLM-Based Audit of Political Neutrality along Ideologies
hook: Grokipedia launched as the 'unbiased' answer to Wikipedia's alleged left-lean. Audited by four LLM judges, including Grok itself, it rates less neutral — just biased the other way.
key_points: Analyzed 1,394 matched article pairs about government figures on Grokipedia and Wikipedia, scored along 9 expert-coded ideology dimensions.
Used 4 different LLM judges (Grok, Claude, Mistral, DeepSeek) to cross-check for judge-specific bias.
Every judge, including Grok, rated Grokipedia as less neutral overall than Wikipedia.

Both encyclopedias favor politicians overall, but along different lines: Grokipedia favors economically right-wing and penalizes socially liberal figures; Wikipedia skews favorably toward socially liberal figures.
content_html: Grokipedia, an encyclopedia written entirely by the LLM Grok, launched in late 2025 partly as an answer to accusations that Wikipedia leans "left-wing." This paper puts that neutrality claim to the test: does an LLM-written encyclopedia actually reduce political bias, or does it just swap in a different one?
extra_html:
Filippos Vlahos, Guillaume Bied, and Tijl De Bie compared 1,394 matched article pairs about government figures across both encyclopedias, scoring each along nine expert-coded ideology dimensions. To guard against any single judge's own leanings, they used four separate LLM judges — Grok, Claude, Mistral, and DeepSeek — and checked whether the judges agreed with each other.

They did: every judge, Grok included, rated Grokipedia as less neutral overall than Wikipedia. Both encyclopedias tend to portray politicians favorably on net, but toward different groups — Grokipedia favors economically right-wing politicians while penalizing socially liberal ones, whereas Wikipedia's favorable tilt runs toward socially liberal figures. The authors, at Ghent University, frame this as evidence that an "unbiased by design" encyclopedia can still encode a strong ideological lean — just a different one from its predecessor. Source: arXiv, arxiv.org/abs/2607.15146.

related.title: A Model's Stance Is a Deployment Setting, Not a Property
related.hook: The same Grok model ID rated a pseudo-scientific claim 75 via API and 5.5 via web. What a commercial LLM 'believes' turns out to be a contingent effect of how it's deployed.

flashcards.prompt: What was Grokipedia's stated motivation, and did the audit's LLM judges agree it delivered on that?
flashcards.back_html: Grokipedia (an encyclopedia written entirely by Grok, launched late 2025) aimed to be a more neutral alternative to Wikipedia — but all four LLM judges, including Grok itself, rated it less neutral than Wikipedia.

flashcards.prompt: Why did the authors use four different LLM judges (Grok, Claude, Mistral, DeepSeek) instead of one?

choices.text: Because the judges themselves could carry their own political biases, so cross-checking across models tests whether findings are judge-specific
Because a single LLM cannot process encyclopedia-length articles
Because only Grok was allowed to score Grokipedia articles

flashcards.explanation_html: Using multiple judges lets the authors separate the encyclopedias' bias from any single judge's own leanings — and the finding (Grokipedia less neutral) held across all four.

flashcards.prompt: How do Grokipedia's and Wikipedia's biases differ, per the study?
flashcards.back_html: Both favor politicians overall, but in opposite directions: Grokipedia favors economically right-wing figures and penalizes socially liberal ones, while Wikipedia is rated as favoring socially liberal figures.
